sections.h2: Your real choices for a fast Denton sale
sections.html:
You can sell a Denton house three ways: through an agent, to a buyer you locate, or to a cash buyer. How soon you need to close, and what shape the roof, kitchen and systems are in, will usually settle it.

The house is taxed and recorded through Denton County. Investors who want rentals compete here with families who want a place to live, and that mix can help if your house is dated or damaged: an investor builds the repair cost into the price rather than making you fix things first.

  • Agent listing: the biggest audience, in exchange for showings, repair requests after inspection and a wait for mortgage approval.
  • Owner sale: you keep the commission and also take on the contract, the disclosure form and the negotiating.
  • Cash purchase: a faster calendar and fewer contingencies, with the discount that comes from buying a house unrepaired.

Denton has an old core. The city counts 69 local historic landmarks across more than seven architectural styles, concentrated along West Oak Street, plus three local historic districts covering over 80 acres on the west and north sides.

If your house is a landmark, exterior changes go through a design review process and demolition needs approval from the Historic Landmark Commission. Designation does not change the zoned use of the property. A renovator will raise this early, so check whether your address carries a local designation before you sign anything. The city's development staff take those questions at development@cityofdenton.com.

Newer subdivisions have no such overlay, and buyers there focus on the roof, the foundation and the age of the mechanical systems. Wherever you live, get repair responsibility in writing.

Anyone who wants a vacation rental needs a city registration. Denton's definition of a short-term rental is renting a whole dwelling unit or a bedroom for at least 24 hours and no more than 29 consecutive days, and every operator must register.

Registration costs $150 and is valid for one calendar year, with applications and renewals filed through the city's STR permit system. Council approved amendments to the Denton Development Code on October 22, 2024, that changed these rules. For the packet and full requirements, call Development Services at (940) 349-8600 or write to building@cityofdenton.com. Violations can carry a maximum penalty of $2,000.

This touches a sale in two ways. If the house is on short stays today, expect the buyer to ask if your registration is current. If a buyer wants to use it that way, the offer depends on rules you cannot promise on their behalf, so send them to the city with the question.

Unpermitted work is the most common surprise, so go through your records before the house goes under contract. Permitting runs through the Development Service Center. As of January 2, 2026 the center closes at noon on Fridays, and Friday afternoon occupied inspections are taken by phone at (940) 349-8195.

Ask for the permit history on your address if you added a room, a deck, a garage conversion or new electrical service. An inspector or lender may ask to see closed permits. If something was built without one, you can still sell, but you will either need to resolve it or accept a lower price from a buyer who takes that risk.

  • Gather receipts and permit numbers for any major work.
  • Call Development Services at (940) 349-8600 to ask about open permits.
  • Tell every buyer about known problems in writing.

sections.h2: How a sale closes after you accept an offer
sections.html:
Expect a title company or an attorney to draft the deed, a notary to watch you sign, and the Denton County clerk to receive the filing, because Texas records a deed where the land is. An unacknowledged deed will be rejected. Ask the closing agent for the clerk's charges and the recording total.

Property tax creates a lien on January 1, and the person who owns the house that day is liable. Late charges begin in February. Most title companies pay the year's tax at closing, so ask the Denton County tax office for your balance in good time.

sections.h2: Inherited, behind on payments or owing back taxes
sections.html:
Each of these has its own deadline. A will can be probated for four years after a death. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement placed on file with the county clerk, and no law forces a buyer to honor it. Because title companies set their own standards of proof, bring it up early.

With a mortgage in arrears, the lender starts with a default notice, and paying the arrears inside 20 days reinstates the loan. A notice of auction comes next, and the sale itself is held on a first Tuesday. Sometimes a cash buyer can close ahead of it.

For back property taxes, ask the Denton County tax office whether the account has gone to a suit. Penalty waivers exist in some cases if you pay promptly and ask in writing, so raise it with the tax office.

A slim folder can save days. Put in the deed, a payoff letter from your lender, the newest tax bill, permit numbers, and the lease if someone rents the house. When appliances are staying, name them in the contract so the final walk-through brings no argument. A few days before you list, ask your title company to look for open liens or permits. You will have time to fix a surprise without a contract deadline bearing down. It also helps to photograph the house in daylight, with the yard and street in frame, so buyers can compare it with newer listings.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to register a short-term rental in Denton?
faqs.a: Yes. Registration costs $150 and is valid for one calendar year. Renewals go through the same STR permit system.

faqs.q: Does Denton require a permit for a house I plan to sell?
faqs.a: The sale itself needs none. Permits cover construction, so look into whether earlier work on your house was permitted, and phone Development Services at (940) 349-8600 if unsure.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax on a Denton house?
faqs.a: Local taxing units set the rates and the county tax office sends the bill, while the appraisal district assigns the value. There is no state property tax in Texas. The Denton County tax office can give you your current balance.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Denton house that has a historic landmark designation?
faqs.a: Yes. Designation does not affect the use of the property, which zoning controls. It does add design review for exterior changes and requires Historic Landmark Commission approval before demolition.

faqs.q: How soon can a cash sale close in Denton?
faqs.a: Whatever date the contract names. Get it in writing, and remember that title work, a probate or lien problem or an unpaid tax bill can push it back.
